stage: HISTORIE (engine stage 6) - fractal axis + competing frames - cache
disputedNote: Even where this story begins is disputed - picking a start date is itself a position. Frames change emphasis and annotation, never the record.

frames.label: April 2025 suspension
frames.note: Under this frame the story begins when India placed the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance after the Pahalgam attack in April 2025, treating water as leverage tied to cross-border terror. The current Pakistani UNSC letter and ministerial warnings read as escalation inside a security crisis that India initiated. This is the frame Indian government sources and Indian outlets such as Business Today open with.

frames.label: June 2026 UNSC letter
frames.note: Under this frame the story begins on 19 June 2026 when Deputy PM Ishaq Dar wrote to the UNSC alleging Indian attempts to alter river flows, alongside Bilawal Bhutto and the defence minister issuing war-tinged warnings. The current row reads as a fresh diplomatic and rhetorical escalation distinct from older treaty history. This is the frame Pakistani outlets Tribune, Geo, Samaa and Daily Excelsior open with.

bands.label: UNSC letter and war rhetoric
bands.summary: Pakistan escalates via a UNSC letter from Dar plus public warnings from Bilawal Bhutto and the defence minister accusing India of weaponising Indus flows.

nodes.title: Dar warns India against using water as a weapon
nodes.what: Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar publicly warns that Indian moves to expand reservoir capacity on the Indus system amount to using water as a weapon. Speaking through Pakistani outlets, he labels the posture hydro-hegemony and ties it to the treaty row that opened after April 2025.

nodes.title: Dar writes to UN Security Council over alleged Indian attempts to alter river flows
nodes.what: Ishaq Dar sends a letter to the UN Security Council requesting action over what Islamabad describes as Indian attempts to alter the flow of Indus system rivers. Pakistani outlets report the letter alongside his stated concerns over ongoing Indian projects on the Indus, framing the move as the first formal multilateral escalation in the current row.

nodes.title: Bilawal Bhutto says Pakistan is ready to respond to India
nodes.what: Pakistan Peoples Party chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari issues public statements over the Indus Waters Treaty row, declaring that Pakistan is ready to respond to India. The remarks add a senior political-party voice to the government's diplomatic letter, broadening the domestic chorus on the water question.
nodes.disputed: Indian commentary describes the remarks as open threats and escalation; Pakistani coverage describes them as a defensive response to Indian moves on the treaty.

nodes.title: Pakistani defence minister signals war-tinged warning over Indus waters
nodes.what: Pakistan's defence minister tells media that there will be a moment Islamabad feels compelled to act, framing a war-tinged warning tied to Indus water flows. Indian outlet Business Today carries the remarks, presenting them as a sharpening of Pakistani rhetoric alongside the UNSC letter and Bilawal's statements.
nodes.disputed: Indian coverage describes the remarks as a war threat; Pakistani officials describe similar statements during this week as conditional warnings tied to Indian actions on the rivers.

bands.label: Treaty in abeyance
bands.summary: India holds the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance after the Pahalgam attack and signals reservoir and project expansion on western rivers.

nodes.title: Pahalgam attack kills tourists in Kashmir
nodes.what: Gunmen attacked tourists at Baisaran meadow near Pahalgam in Indian-administered Kashmir, killing 26 people. India attributed the assault to militants backed from across the border, while Pakistan rejected involvement and called for a neutral investigation.
nodes.disputed: Indian authorities described it as a cross-border terror attack with Pakistani links; Pakistani officials described it as an internal Kashmir security incident with no proven Pakistani role.

nodes.title: India places Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance
nodes.what: India's Cabinet Committee on Security announced that the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty would be held in abeyance until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably renounces cross-border terrorism. The step came alongside closure of the Attari-Wagah crossing and downgrading of diplomatic ties.

nodes.title: Pakistan calls treaty move an act of war
nodes.what: Pakistan's National Security Committee met and declared that any attempt to stop or divert waters allocated to Pakistan under the treaty would be considered an act of war. Islamabad also suspended the Simla Agreement and closed its airspace to Indian carriers.

nodes.title: India launches Operation Sindoor
nodes.what: India conducted missile and air strikes on sites it identified as militant infrastructure inside Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir. Pakistan reported civilian casualties and responded with strikes of its own, opening four days of the most intense military exchange between the two states in decades.
nodes.disputed: India described the strikes as precision counter-terror action; Pakistan described them as unprovoked attacks on civilian areas.

nodes.title: Ceasefire holds, treaty stays suspended
nodes.what: After missile, drone and artillery exchanges, India and Pakistan announced a ceasefire understanding. Indian officials made clear the Indus Waters Treaty would remain in abeyance regardless of the military pause, linking water to the wider terror question.

nodes.title: Reservoir flushing on the Chenab
nodes.what: India reportedly carried out reservoir flushing and de-silting at the Baglihar and Salal dams on the Chenab without the prior notification the treaty had required. Indian officials signalled accelerated work on storage and hydro projects on the western rivers earlier reserved for Pakistan's use.

nodes.title: Indian leadership rules out restoring the treaty
nodes.what: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah publicly stated that the Indus Waters Treaty would not be restored, with Shah saying water once flowing to Pakistan would be redirected for Indian use. Pakistani officials condemned the statements as violations of an international agreement.
